2010_005_050410regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, May 4, 2010, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. The business calendar carried a flooring replacement award to Conventional Carpet in the amount of $953,323.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, a fall athletic supplies bid totaling $23,677.24 split among ten vendors, and the appointment of Janet Keeling as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction effective July 1, 2010. Reports covered the 2009-2010 student survey, a proposed weighted grade point average for Advanced Placement courses, and Oakland Schools' proposed fiscal year 2010-11 budgets.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, May 4, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000.

**Recognition**
Pamela (Pam) Byrd, Secretary at Hamilton Elementary School, was named recipient of the 2009-2010 Outstanding Support Staff Award, selected from nine nominations by a committee of TESA (Troy Educational Secretaries Association), TESPA (Troy Educational Support Personnel Association), and non-represented personnel. Byrd started as a Teacher's Assistant in September of 1995 and has served as a Secretary since May of 1999.

**Consent agenda**
Item A, minutes of the April 20, 2010 Board of Education meeting; Item B, awarding of the bid for fall athletic supplies.

**Fall athletic supplies (Bid #9665)**

**Personnel**
Recommended appointment of Janet Keeling as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective July 1, 2010. Keeling was hired as a teacher in November 1977, became principal at Morse Elementary in 1988 and at Bemis Elementary in 1999.

**Curriculum reports**
Results of the district student survey, presented by Stuart Redpath and Anne Mull of the Department of Instruction and Assessment. Students in grades 3-12 were surveyed February 8 to February 11, 2010, with separate forms for grades 3-5 (N=2,385), 6-8 (N=2,659), and 9-12 (N=3,407).

High school graduation requirements and GPA calculations, presented by Richard Machesky, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction: beginning with the class of 2014, full-year world language courses taken before ninth grade count toward Michigan Merit Curriculum and district graduation requirements; participation in the Michigan Merit Exam is required for graduation; and a weighted grading system for Advanced Placement courses beginning with the class of 2011.

**Oakland ISD budget report**
Michael Adamczyk presented Oakland Schools' proposed fiscal year 2010-11 budgets under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, which requires each ISD to submit its budget to constituent districts by May 1 and each local board to adopt a supporting or disapproving resolution by June 1. Total revenue is budgeted at $323.9 Million against a total expenditure budget of $351.7 Million.

**Closed session**
Consideration of the superintendent's evaluation under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a).

**Meeting and agenda.** Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting, Tuesday, May 04, 2010, 7:00 PM, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August. The agenda ran: Pledge of Allegiance; Recognition (Outstanding Support Staff Person of the Year); Additions & Deletions; Public Communication (agenda items); General-Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda items); Other; Closed Session; Adjournment.

**Recognition - 2009-2010 Outstanding Support Staff Award.** In conjunction with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association (TESA) and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association (TESPA), all employees were invited to nominate candidates. A committee of TESA, TESPA, and non-represented personnel selected Pam Byrd, Secretary at Hamilton Elementary School, as the overall winner from nine nominations. The resolution recites that Pam Byrd started as a Teacher's Assistant for the Troy School District in September of 1995 and has served as a Secretary since May of 1999, and commends Pamela Byrd for her selection and exceptional service; signed this fourth day of May, 2010.

**Consent agenda (Item 5).** A. Minutes of the April 20, 2010 Board of Education meeting. B. Awarding of Bid for Fall Athletic Supplies.

**Minutes of April 20, 2010.** President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. in the Services Building. Present in addition to Ms. Underwood were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, and Pochodylo; also present were Superintendent Fowler, administrators Adamczyk, Bryan, Davisson, Jolly, Machesky, McAvoy, and Witt, and approximately 52 additional members of the audience. The Board recognized winter all-state athletes: George Abro (Senior, Athens High School, wrestling 145 lb weight class, Coach Mario Bastianelli); Sara Lin (Sophomore, Troy High School, gymnastics, Coach Cynthia Tan); Brooke Madzia (Senior, Athens High School, gymnastics, Allstate 2010, 2009, 2008, repeat state champion in the All-Around for Division 2, state champion on the vault, broke the state record for floor exercises, Coach Deanna Fakhouri); Miles McDonald (Sophomore, Troy High School, boys' swimming, Coach Jason Cavicchioli); Jacqlynn Stewart (Junior, Athens High School, gymnastics, Coach Deanna Fakhouri); and Jeremy Stoian (Senior, Athens High School, wrestling 130 lb weight class, 2x County Champion, Coach Mario Bastianelli). The Board also acknowledged 47 senior scholar athletes from winter and spring sports, a distinction requiring a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program. President Underwood called a brief recess at 7:11 p.m.; the meeting reconvened at 7:18 p.m. Mr. Bruce Bloomingdale, a Troy School District resident, addressed the Board regarding his opposition to the proposed new Board policy for public participation at Board of Education meetings.

**April 20 actions.** Resolution 10-032, moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved consent items A, minutes of the March 16, 2010 meeting; B, Treasurer's Report for March, 2010; and C, awarding of bid for Library Automation Software (Yes 7, No 0). Personnel recommendations, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, included retirements of Jean Brazelton-McGehee (Hamilton), Kathleen Danielson (Niles Community High School), Jane Drotos (Hamilton), Ruth Frushour (Athens), Michael Heist (Boulan Park), Janis Hodgkins (Larson), Jane Juett (Leonard), Monica Lamb (Hamilton), Rosalie Mallory (Troy Union), Rosemary Morrow (Troy High), Leon Raczkowski (Costello), Linda Ruks (Boulan Park), and Alan Walthall (Boulan Park), previously accepted by Dr. Fowler per Board policy and effective at the end of the school day on June 21, 2010 (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-033, moved by Mrs. Edmunds and supported by Mrs. Philippart, accepted the resignation of Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent-Business Services, effective June 30, 2010 (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-034, moved by Mrs. Pochodylo and supported by Mr. Miletti, awarded tenure status to Josh Heppner (Athens High School), Kathryn Amaradio-Taylor (Baker Middle School), Andrea Lothian (Larson Middle School), Christine Russell (Morse Elementary School), Kelly Paterson (International Academy-East), and Shannon Tonkin (International Academy-East) (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-035, moved by Mrs. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Edmunds, approved reductions in certified staff due to the projected financial condition of the School District and proposed budget reductions for the 2010/2011 fiscal year, naming among others Omar Hakim, Krysta Gentilini, Gareth Eve, Josh Pudaloff, Ryan Fisher, Emily Beski, Shannon Kraegel, Amanda Ellul, Katie Owczarek, Fen Xing, Stephanie Peterson, Stephen Gallagher, Danielle Szachta, Megan Phillips, Cynthia Christiansen, Mark Cavataio, Joslin John, Chad Gurzick, Stacey Miller, Nicholas Kolbe, Eric Andary, Andrea Alter, Emily Davidson, Jessica Cooper, Daniel Adler, Jennifer Zablocki, Susan Flewelling, Carolyn Murtagh, Katherine Hyso, Lori Carmichael, Ronald Lawson, Angelika Gadlage, Erin Reinhart, Lindsey Gerbe, Michelle Tessoff, Karey Hansen, Krystina Weiss, Michele Marszalkowski, Erin Johnson, Candice Tamakloe, Vivek Nayak, Marisa Contrera, Bahia Farhat-Rouvalis, Judy Coster, Karyn Schachinger, Janet Herberholz, Jody Smith, Sandra Lewallen, Jenna Thompson, Mallory Schueller, Jessica Thudium, Emily Bard, Michelle Sloan, Mary Farran, Meiyu Chang, Jodi Steimel, Michael Hosbach, Nichole Vasu, Andrew La Torre, Tabitha Shaw, April Muller, Sean Fisher, Kathryn Robles, Monica Petrous, Andrea Bolterstein, and Mary Bruss (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-036, moved by Mr. Miletti and supported by Mrs. Fleming, adopted the Teen Health textbook support materials, including the human sexuality information, published by Glencoe, presented at the March 16, 2010 meeting, for the middle school health program as an expenditure of the 2010/2011 secondary textbook budgets in the estimated amount of $17,193 (Yes 7, No 0). A further resolution, moved by Mrs. Philippart and supported by Mr. Hauff, awarded the bid for document cameras to City Automation in the amount of $29,850.00 as an expenditure of the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 10-038, moved by Mr. Edmunds and supported by Mrs. Fleming, approved changes to Board policies B-1208 Voting, B-1211 Public Participation in Board of Education Meetings, B-1301 Agenda Format for Regular Meetings, C-1402 Smoking Policy, K-1303 Political and/or Commercial Advertising by District Employees, K-1304 Advertising on School Property and in School District Electronic Media, and new Board policy D-1106 Fixed Assets, following a second reading (Yes 7, No 0). Andrew Michail, student representative from Troy High School, reported on Activist Week: Monday awareness day, Tuesday "Reuse a Shoe Day," Wednesday "Support Our Troops" day, Thursday "Green Day," and Friday "Canned Food Day." Mrs. Pochodylo reported that she, Mrs. Philippart, Dr. Fowler, and Tim McAvoy spent time with Representative Marty Knollenberg and Senator John Pappageorge; Mrs. Philippart reported attending the Governor's Summit on Education in Lansing. The meeting was adjourned at 8:10 p.m. on a motion by Mrs. Philippart supported by Mr. Miletti. Minutes submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary (NLP:sc).

**Fall athletic supplies, Bid Award #9665.** Bids were opened April 1, 2010 for various supplies for the fall athletic program; bids were sent to 17 potential bidders with 13 responding, none of which were "No Bid." Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052, fax 248-823-4077), reviewed the results with Athletic Director M. The 16-page bid tabulation for 2010/11 Fall Athletic Equipment covers Athens Football, Athens Boys Soccer, Athens Boys Water Polo, Troy High Football, Troy High Cross Country, Troy High Volleyball, Baker Football, Baker Boys Basketball, Larson Football, Smith Football, and Smith Middle School, and includes non-awarded bidders S & S Worldwide, Bill Fritz Sports, and Aluminum Athletic Equip. Coast to Coast Sports, Flaghouse, M-F Athletic Co., and Tri-County Custom Sports were recorded as No Response.

**Personnel - administrative appointment.** The Superintendent recommended the appointment of Janet Keeling as Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction. Mrs. Keeling was hired as a teacher in the district in November 1977, became a building principal at Morse Elementary in 1988 and then Bemis Elementary in 1999. The suggested resolution issues a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position, with duties beginning July 1, 2010.

**Curriculum - results of student survey.** Presented by Stuart Redpath and Anne Mull of the Troy School District Department of Instruction and Assessment, addressing the district continuous improvement goal that all students perceive they are accepted at school regardless of cultural, ethnic, gender, academic, or other individual differences, as measured by a validated survey. Students in grades 3-12 were surveyed, with different forms for grades 3-5, 6-8, and 9-12; the survey window was open from February 8th to February 11th, 2010, and individual responses are confidential. Grades 3-5 respondents numbered N=2,385, drawn from Barnard Elementary 237 (9.9%), Bemis 215 (9.0%), Costello 156 (6.5%), Hamilton 202 (8.5%), Hill 170 (7.1%), Leonard 252 (10.6%), Martell 173 (7.3%), Morse 194 (8.1%), Schroeder 201 (8.4%), Troy Union 218 (9.1%), Wass 174 (7.3%), and Wattles 182 (7.6%); by racial-ethnic identification, Asian 662 (27.8%), Black 119 (5.0%), Hispanic 28 (1.2%), Multiracial 107 (4.5%), and White 1453 (60.9%). Grades 6-8 respondents numbered N=2,659: Baker Middle School 650 (24.4%), Boulan 673 (25.3%), Larson 673 (25.3%), Smith 663 (24.9%); Black 129 (4.9%), Arabic 95 (3.6%), Asian 683 (25.7%), White 1374 (51.7%), Chaldean 83 (3.1%), Hispanic 53 (2.0%), Multiracial 176 (6.6%); 4-Year College was the after-high-school plan of 1789 (67.3%). Grades 9-12 respondents numbered N=3,407: Athens High School 1426 (41.9%), Niles Community HS 131 (3.8%), Troy High School 1850 (54.3%); Black 172 (5.0%), Arabic 107 (3.1%), Asian 628 (18.4%), White 1892 (55.5%), Chaldean 142 (4.2%), Hispanic 70 (2.1%), Native American 27 (0.8%), Multiracial 156 (4.6%); 1935 (56.8%) had been in Troy schools 8 years or more and 2553 (74.9%) named 4-Year College. Year-over-year slides compared 2008-2009 with 2009-2010 agree/strongly agree percentages: for grades 3-5 on "I am accepted by other students at my school," Black responses moved from 63 to 73 and Hispanic from 71 to 75, and on "I feel safe at school" Black moved from 76 to 83 and Hispanic from 85 to 93. Next steps stated that each school will be provided with its own building data sets and that results will be used for continuous improvement.

**Curriculum - graduation requirements and GPA.** Reported by Richard Machesky, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, in a Board of Education Report dated May 4, 2010. Beginning with the class of 2014, full year world language courses taken by students prior to ninth grade will count toward having met the Michigan Merit Curriculum and Troy School District graduation requirements; such courses include, but may not be limited to, Chinese 1, French 1, German 1, Japanese 1, and Spanish 1. Participation in the Michigan Merit Exam is required for graduation. Several highly competitive school districts have or are moving toward a grading system with a weighting factor for Advanced Placement (AP) courses, and highly competitive colleges have indicated they will no longer recalculate grade point averages for determining college acceptance and scholarships. An ad-hoc committee met and made a recommendation to the HSCC that a weighted grading system be adopted, that the district determine whether it should be prospective, retroactive, or both, that it apply to AP courses only, and that expanding honors points beyond AP be discussed during the 2010-2011 school year. Beginning with the class of 2011, students who have taken AP courses would have weighted values added to their cumulative GPA at the conclusion of each course: against a current scale of A = 4.0, B = 3.0, C = 2.0, D = 1.0, E = 0, the recommended AP scale is A = 5.0 (1.0), B = 3.75, C = 2.50, D = 1.25, E = 0. Two illustrations used a Total Number of Classes Taken of 24: in the first, all A's (4) totaling 96 with 4 AP classes taken produced a current GPA of 96/24 = 4.0 versus a weighted GPA of 100/24 = 4.166; in the second, 20 A = 80 plus 4 B = 12 totaling 92 produced a current GPA of 92/24 = 3.83 with 0 AP classes versus a weighted GPA of 95/24 = 3.96 with 4 AP classes (4 x .75 = 3.0).

Column totals were $953,323.00, $155,140.00, and $549,147.75. Fair Way Tile & Carpet, Floorcraft Floor Covering, Imperial Floor Covering, Metro Wholesale Flooring, Quality Floor Covering, and Tri-County Floor Covering were recorded as No Response.

**Business - proposed Oakland Intermediate School District budget.** Effective in 2004, Section 624 of the Revised School Code (380.624) requires every Intermediate School District to submit a copy of its budget to local school districts no later than May 1, and local districts to pass a resolution in support or disapproval no later than June 1, mailing a copy of the resolution to the Oakland Schools Board of Education. Michael M. Adamczyk transmitted the Oakland Schools PowerPoint in an April 27, 2010 memorandum to Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. (4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098-4777, 248.823.4010, fax 248.823.4013), noting detailed line item budgets for Oakland Schools' General Fund, Special Education Fund, Debt Service Funds, Capital Projects Funds, Enterprise Fund, and Internal Service Fund are available in his office. Revenue assumptions: property tax revenue decrease of 13%, with further declines of 12% in 2011-12 and 5% in 2012-13, flat in 2013-14, and 2% growth in 2014-15; expected investment rate of return of 1.5%; General Education Section 81 reduced by 14.5%; fee based service revenues expected to grow by 2.0%. Total revenue for FY 2011 is $323.9 Million. Expenditure assumptions: MPSERS retirement rate budgeted at the weighted average rate of 18.793% (19.41% effective October 1, 2010); non-union health care cost at an annual increase of 13%; union health care subject to an annual cost sharing cap of 6%; Purchased Services reduced by 5%, Supplies & Materials by 10%, Dues & Fees by 10%; utilities reflecting a 6.27% decrease; and total FTE of 105.5 eliminated through attrition, transfers, workforce reduction, and a one-time Voluntary Employee Sick Leave Payout Program (VESLPP) expected to save approximately $9.5 million annually. The total expenditure budget by type is $351.7 Million. The General Education Fund shows total revenue of $17.5 Million (property tax $10.6 M, 60% of total revenue; other local $3.5 M; state sources $2.9 M; other financing sources $.5 M) and total expenditures of $17.7 Million (general administration $1.7 M; finance and operations $7.2 M; instructional services $8.7 M; plant and fixed charges and transfers to LEAs $.1 M), an operating deficit of ($187,700), and a net decrease of (24.63) FTE. Its five-year forecast lists revenue of 17,485,300; 16,438,850; 17,525,423; 16,266,017; and 17,496,124 against expenditures of 17,673,000; 17,520,690; 17,419,037; 17,578,308; and 17,746,829, with unreserved/designated balances of 3,614,900; 2,345,360; 2,451,745; 1,139,454; and 888,749 and end-of-year unreserved fund balance percentages of 19.19%, 13.39%, 14.08%, 6.48%, and 5.01%. The Special Education Fund shows total revenue of $142.0 Million (property tax $134.9 M, 95% of total revenue; other local $1.4 M; state sources $5.7 M) and total expenditures of $153.0 Million (program supervision and direction $2.3 M; program operations $7.5 M; plant and fixed charges $5.7 M; LEA transfers and program subsidies $137.5 M, a decrease of (12.43%) or ($19,525,000) from 2009-2010), an operating deficit of ($11.0) million, and a net decrease of (23.95) FTE. Fiscal Year 2011 Special Education Program Support & Subsidies comprise PA-18 Base Distribution $134,332,100; Start-up Contingency $850,000; Extraordinary Contingency $250,000; Section 24 subsidy $100,000; Group Homes $1,200,000; Havenwick $150,000; SEI Regional Day Treatment $450,000; and Michigan Rehab Services Cash Match $180,000, totaling $137,512,100, with the PA-18 Base Distribution noted as an $(8.8m) decline from FY 2010. The Special Education five-year forecast lists revenue of 142,044,900; 125,951,499; 120,248,596; 120,541,458; and 123,130,206 against expenditures of 153,016,800; 125,868,753; 120,153,830; 120,432,549; and 123,021,792, a reserved center program facility renovation balance rising from 286,000 to 686,000, and an end-of-year unreserved fund balance percentage net of LEA O.T. of 5.00% in every year. The Career Focused Education Fund shows total revenue of $34.1 Million (property tax $33.0 M, 96% of total revenue; other local $0.6 M; state sources $.4 M; other financing sources $0.1 M) and total expenditures of $32.9 Million (campus and other program administration $21.8 M; LEA transfers and direct program operations $5.1 M; facility and technology maintenance/renovations $0.1 M; plant and fixed charges $5.9 M), with a net decrease of (56.92) FTE; its five-year forecast lists revenue of 34,195,900; 30,312,556; 28,917,591; 28,985,006; and 30,100,462 against expenditures of 32,910,900; 32,087,848; 30,524,315; 30,949,980; and 31,323,685, unreserved fund balances of 8,137,000; 6,361,708; 4,754,985; 2,790,011; and 1,566,787, and fund balance percentages of 24.72%, 19.83%, 15.58%, 9.01%, and 5.00%. Grants and funded projects carry a total dollar award value of $113.7 Million, with New Awards of $94.5 Million, Carry Over of $19.2 Million, direct transfer to districts of $88 Million, and ISD administered grants and projects of $25.7 Million including JobLink at $11.8M. Fiscal Year 2011 district debt comprises GEF debt principal of $5,165,000 with an average annual payment of $750,000; CFEF debt principal of $44,770,000 with $3,100,000; new QSCB debt principal (funds) of $14,800,000 with $850,000; and total Oakland Schools bonded debt of $64,735,000 with an average annual payment of $4,700,000, with debt service for the Administration Building Project Bond (2003) and the QSCB issue pre-funded in Debt Service Funds 310 and 313 and the 2007 campus renovations bond pre-funded in Debt Service Fund 312 through FY 2014. Other funds listed include Cooperative Activities Funds 270 (CPDI), 271 (Oakland Network for Education, ONE), 272 (Alternative Education High School, under study), and 273 (Medicaid); Debt Service Fund 310 (Administrative Building Bond 2003, 15 years, ending 2018), Fund 312 (CFE Campus Renovations Bond, 29 years, ending 2036), and Fund 313 (Qualified School Construction Bond, 17 years, ending 2027); Capital Projects Funds 404, 406, and 408; Production Print Fund 710 (subsidy eliminated); and Risk Related Activity Fund 810 (unemployment pre-funded).

**Closed session.** The Board was asked to resolve that, as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(a), it go into closed session to discuss the superintendent's evaluation.
